name: Novis case
comment: The second grammar rule:ide/case-files-have-their-own-grammar asks for: the sections of a `.nvst` or `.lspt` case, with Novis embedded in the four that hold a program. It is a thin wrapper — the language patterns are `source.nvs`'s, included rather than restated. The section roster is `crates/nvs-test/src/lib.rs`'s module doc for `.nvst` and `crates/nvs-lsp/src/lib.rs`'s for `.lspt`; a section neither names is left alone, so a header this file has not heard of stays plain text rather than being coloured as one it knows.

file-at-path.comment: `--FILE <relative/path>--` is its own rule rather than an alternative of `#program-section`, because its header carries an argument: the path the body is written to. It is offered the position first, since `#program-section`'s `FILE` is followed immediately by its closing `--` and would not match this header anyway — the order is what a reader expects, not what the regex needs.

program-section.comment: The three headers whose body is a Novis program written without an argument. `--FILE--` is the case itself; `--SKIPIF--` and `--CLEAN--` are the runner's own scaffolding and are always `nvs run`, which is why they are the same shape here.

format-section.comment: The two sections `crates/nvs-test/src/expect.rs` compares with escapes rather than byte for byte. Everything else in them is still literal: what is coloured is the twelve escapes that table names and nothing else, so a `%` standing for itself is left as the byte it is rather than being marked as an escape that does not exist.

text-section.comment: Every other section either format names. The body is literal — an expectation is compared byte for byte and colouring part of it would suggest the runner reads it as something. Only the delimiter is coloured, which is what tells a reader where one section ends. The longer spellings come first in the alternation so `EXPECT-ERROR` is read whole rather than as `EXPECT` followed by bytes that are not `--`.

case-code.comment: Code mode inside one section. The openers are `source.nvs`'s, matched the same way and carrying the same scopes, so an embedded program looks exactly like the file it would be on its own — but the rule is written here rather than included from `source.nvs#code-mode` because of its `end`: a case almost never closes with `?>`, and a rule that ends only there would swallow every section after this one. Ending at the next header as well is what keeps a `--FILE--` with no closing tag from colouring the whole rest of the file as code. The body is `source.nvs#code` itself, so a construct family lands once.
case-code.name: meta.embedded.block.nvs
